title: Gotu kola tincture for mental clarity
subtitle: A leaf tincture for focus, sustained concentration, and cognitive fatigue
excerpt: Dried gotu kola leaf macerated in 40% vodka for four to six weeks, used as a tincture for mental clarity, sustained concentration, and cognitive fatigue. Two to three ml in water twice daily. Course limit is three months, then a break of at least a month: this herb carries a caution for prolonged use and the liver. Not for use in pregnancy.
sourceNotes: WHO monograph on Centella asiatica (1999) : pharmacological properties, traditional uses. Bradwejn et al. (2000), Journal of Clinical Psychopharmacology : clinical study on cognitive function. EMA HMPC monograph on Centella asiatica (2012) : traditional-use framing, safety including liver caution for prolonged use. Tincture preparation conventions follow British Herbal Pharmacopoeia folk-tincture method. Liver caution for prolonged use based on isolated case reports reviewed in EMA assessment.

recipe.yieldDescription: About 120 ml tincture (approximately 40 doses at 3 ml each)
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Maceration takes 4 to 6 weeks. The finished tincture keeps 2 years in dark glass.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Store in amber glass in a cool dark cupboard. Keeps 2 years from the strain date.

glossaryTerms.definition: A preparation in which plant material is macerated in alcohol (usually 40% spirit) to extract both water-soluble and fat-soluble constituents. The alcohol also acts as a preservative, giving the preparation a shelf life of two years or more.

projectSchedule.title: Start your tincture
projectSchedule.body: Pack the dried gotu kola leaf into a clean maceration jar. Pour over the 40% vodka until the herb is fully submerged with at least 2 cm of liquid above. Seal tightly and label with the herb name, the spirit percentage, and today's date. Store in a cool dark cupboard.

projectSchedule.title: Check the liquid level
projectSchedule.body: Open the jar and check the vodka still covers the herb. Top up with a little more 40% vodka if the level has dropped. Shake gently and return to the cupboard.

projectSchedule.title: Taste and check colour
projectSchedule.body: Taste a few drops from a small spoon. The tincture should be mild and slightly grassy with a faint bitterness. The liquid should be a pale green-brown. Return to the cupboard for another two weeks.

projectSchedule.title: Strain and bottle
projectSchedule.body: Your tincture is ready. Line a sieve with a double layer of muslin over a clean jug. Pour through and press the spent herb firmly. Funnel into amber dropper bottles and label.

content.text: is dried gotu kola leaf macerated in 40% vodka for four to six weeks. It is used as a longer-term preparation for mental clarity, sustained concentration, and the kind of cognitive fatigue that comes from sustained mental effort or from recovering after illness. Gotu kola has centuries of use in Ayurvedic and Chinese medicine, and a growing place in western herbal practice for nervous system support. The

path gives a more concentrated preparation than a daily infusion and suits a defined three-month course. The ratio is one part dried leaf to five parts 40% spirit by weight. The course has a hard limit: three months, then a break of at least one month. This herb carries a caution for prolonged use and the liver.

attrs.title: Precautions
attrs.body: Not medical advice. Consult a qualified herbalist or doctor for ongoing or serious symptoms. Pregnancy: consult a herbalist or your midwife before using gotu kola tincture in pregnancy. Liver caution: use is limited to three months at a time. Take a break of at least one month before starting another course. Isolated case reports of liver stress with prolonged use of gotu kola preparations mean this herb is not for indefinite daily use. If you develop any unusual fatigue, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or upper right abdominal discomfort while taking this tincture, stop and see a doctor. No significant drug interactions at standard tincture doses have been documented.

Two to three ml (two to three droppers full) in a small glass of water, twice daily. Morning and afternoon work well. Course: three months maximum, then a break of at least one month. Do not use this herb continuously without a break.
Store in amber glass dropper bottles in a cool, dark cupboard. Keeps two years from the strain date.
When not to use this remedy

Do not use beyond three months without a break. Do not use in pregnancy without first consulting a herbalist or your midwife. Stop and see a doctor if you develop any yellowing of the skin, unusual fatigue, or upper abdominal discomfort while on this
. See a GP for focus difficulty with memory loss, cognitive changes that are sudden, or any cognitive concern that persists beyond what a herbal preparation might address.
